stem.en: A student has ₹100 and must choose between buying a notebook now or saving the money to buy a tennis racket later. Which economic concept best explains this situation?

text.en: Demand — the notebook is cheaper, so more students buy it.
Opportunity cost — giving up the racket for now.
Production — the shop must decide how many notebooks to stock.
Inflation — prices will rise and shrink the value of the ₹100.

explanation.en: Money is limited, so the student must pick one of two wants. Whichever is chosen, the other is given up: that is the opportunity cost (b). Demand is about how much buyers want to buy (a), production is about making goods (c), and inflation is a general rise in prices (d). None of them names what this student gives up.

hints.en: Ask what the student gives up by buying the notebook now.
